public_rationale: The White House's July 23, 2025 announcement linked AI leadership to economic competitiveness [e1]. Google described Gemini 3 as a step toward AGI on November 18, 2025 [e2]. These statements provide context for the impression, but do not establish a collective institutional belief that LLMs will produce AGI and transform the economy [e1, e2]. Assessing the qualified phrase 'appear to be completely smitten' would require adding a definition of institutional scope and a measurable threshold.
limitations: The White House announcement does not establish a specific belief that LLMs will lead to AGI [e1].
Google's statement does not establish a collective attitude across Silicon Valley [e2].
These contextual examples cannot supply the missing threshold for the impression or establish that it is wrong.

statement.excerpt: Silicon Valley and The White House appear to be completely smitten with large language models, rebuilding the world around the hope that LLMs will lead to artificial general intelligence, and a radically redefined economy.

rebuilding the world around the hope

our_interpretation: The sentence offers a qualified impression of institutional enthusiasm at the time of publication, December 23, 2025.
The hope about AGI and economic transformation is attributed to others; it is not Marcus's own forecast.
Public statements and actions can establish grounds for that impression, but converting them into a binary test of being 'completely smitten' would add a commitment and threshold he did not supply.
The plain-reading exception for firm claims does not apply to this qualified characterization.
criteria.support_condition: No determinate support condition preserves the wording as written. Statements endorsing AGI ambitions and transformative AI policies can provide context for the impression, without establishing an objective threshold for it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No determinate contradiction condition preserves the wording as written. Reservations or contrary examples could qualify the impression but would not necessarily falsify what these institutions 'appear' to believe.
